doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

title: Buddy Fisher's band and Basie's nickname F Sharp Henderson
summary: Playing Kansas City with Buddy Fisher, he met Basie at the Reno Club and was nicknamed F Sharp Henderson; a later concert with Ella and Basie.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Yeah, that would be it, yeah. I played with three or four of those bands. Unbelievable. They were all bad, but this was a great learning process. In fact I played with a band, his name was Buddy Fisher, another — he imitated Ben Burney. I don’t know how he ever came about that but he talked and he spoke lyrics and thought he was such a star in front of the band. And we played Kansas City at the Muhlbach Hotel and I went down to the very famous street and met a guy by the name of Bill Basie, who had a seven piece band in the Reno Club. And I remember that I don’t remember who it was in the band, but somebody wanted to play something in the key of G, which was unheard of that you’d play sharps, because they played E flat, B flat, F, C, that was it. Maybe three flats, yeah E flat. Maybe A flat, or as a big chord, a D flat. But something like that. But anyway, I could play in the key of G and that astounded Basie, that I could read in sharp keys. And then for the rest of my life, and Ruth, my wife and I loved Bill very much, he called me

“F Sharp Henderson.” That was my name, the rest of my life, wherever I would see him. We did a concert once with the San Antonio Symphony, which was one of the greatest memories of my life, believe it or not with Ella and she was on — Ella, Bill Basie’s band, and quite a decent period with the San Antonio orchestra. It was one of the greatest nights, music nights, I just sat there like you’re living in Valhalla, but nobody came. I couldn’t believe it. It was a benefit but they put up a sign and said here they are, but we had a very small house as they say so the promoter was less than friendly with us. But what a musical night we had.
Too bad it didn’t get recorded, right?
Oh that would have been so wonderful.
F Sharp Henderson, but only from Bill.
I heard his key was F or —
